(1) B779270c994: split_diff keeps the newline with a file's header, so a file larger than max_chunk_chars is never sent as a header-only chunk (R1dc7a03312). data.body: Part 1 (B-fix-review-chunks, merged bde10e6) names every unreviewed chunk with its files. Part 2: a deterministic truncation of one chunk forced re-running the WHOLE review (25-40 min) or bypassing ddflow with an unverifiable out-of-band call (home-simulator 34.8f). Design: (1) evidence of every ddflow review gains diff_sha (sha256 of the hunk-context-stripped diff), max_chunk_chars, reviewed (chunk numbers) and findings with their chunk number (detail capped). (2) 'ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk N' (repeatable, or '2,5'); MCP ddflow_review 'chunks'. Chunk numbers are those the last run printed; only those chunks are sent. (3) The result MERGES with the gate's latest record only when that record is a ddflow review of the SAME diff_sha, max_chunk_chars and reviewer; otherwise refused (exit 3) with 'run the full review: the diff or chunking changed'. Merged: reviewed = union; findings = earlier chunks' kept + re-run chunks' replaced; unreviewed = the rest with their earlier reasons; outcome recomputed as a full run would. (4) A chunk number outside 1..N refused. Tests: tests/test_review_rechunk.py. Waits for cli.py/mcp.py (held by B-fix-globs-surfaces at filing time).

chunk_findings.detail: `_rerun_scope` validates the recorded chunking by reading `prior.get("chunk_chars")`, but the evidence schema described for this change (and used everywhere else in this same function: `diff_sha`, `reviewed`) records that value under `max_chunk_chars` — the name also used on the reviewer object (`mine[0].max_chunk_chars`) and in the intent. With a full review that wrote its evidence as `max_chunk_chars`, `prior.get("chunk_chars")` is `None`, so the test `mine[0].max_chunk_chars != prior.get("chunk_chars")` is always true and every `--chunk` request is refused with "the chunks differ, run the full review". Example: reviewer has `max_chunk_chars = 40000`; the recorded review stored `{"diff_sha": "...", "max_chunk_chars": 40000, "reviewed": [1,2], ...}`; `prior.get("chunk_chars")` returns `None`, `40000 != None`, so `ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk 1` exits 3 even though the diff and chunking are unchanged — the feature this change exists to enable never merges. Either the reader must look up `prior.get("max_chunk_chars")` or the writer must store the key the reader consults; as written the two names do not agree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:_rerun_scope

chunk_findings.detail: The change removes the documented `extra_rules: str = ""` parameter from `run_review` and drops the line that folded it into the reviewer prompt (`rules = "\n\n".join(r.strip() for r in (rev.extra_rules, extra_rules) ...)`), replacing it with `only: list[int] | None = None` while the render call now uses only `rev.extra_rules.strip()`. This is a breaking change with two concrete failure modes: (1) any existing caller that still passes `extra_rules=...` (e.g. a `--extra-rules` flag or api wrapper) now raises `TypeError: run_review() got an unexpected keyword argument 'extra_rules'`, breaking `ddflow review`; (2) a caller passing it positionally (it sat immediately after `prompt_overrides`, exactly where `only` now sits) silently binds the rules string to `only`, after which `outside = [n for n in wanted if not 1 <= n <= len(chunks)]` evaluates `1 <= 's'` and raises `TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str'`. Even if every caller were migrated, caller-supplied review rules are now silently discarded rather than merged, which no part of the stated design mentions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:1377 (run_review signature / rules rendering)

chunk_findings.detail: The change's own contract (items 1 and 3) says the recorded evidence gains `max_chunk_chars` and that the merge is allowed "only when that record is a ddflow review of the SAME diff\_sha, `max_chunk_chars` and reviewer". But `merge_rerun` compares `prior.get("chunk_chars")` (and names the tuple entry `"chunk_chars"`), i.e. it reads a key that the recorded evidence does not contain. Given a prior full-review record such as `{"reviewer": "claude", "diff_sha": "…", "max_chunk_chars": 4096, "reviewed": [1,2,3], …}` and a matching re-run, the middle iteration evaluates `prior.get("chunk_chars") != res.chunk_chars` → `None != 4096` → `True`, so `merge_rerun` immediately returns the refusal string ("the recorded review differs in chunk\_chars (None vs 4096), …"). The CLI then exits 3 with "run the full review: the diff or chunking changed" even though the diff, chunking and reviewer are identical. The net effect is that no `ddflow review <id> --chunk N` call can ever merge, which is exactly the 25–40 min full re-run (or out-of-band model call) this change exists to eliminate; the feature is dead on arrival. The other two comparisons (`reviewer`, `diff_sha`) match the attribute/record names, so the asymmetry on the chunk-size key is the defect. The fix is to compare the recorded `max_chunk_chars` (e.g. `("max_chunk_chars", res.chunk_chars)`, or rename the stored field consistently in both the writer and this reader).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py — `merge_rerun` guard loop (`("chunk_chars", res.chunk_chars)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `"diff changed" in out.reason` (line ~`assert out.exit == REFUSED and "diff changed" in out.reason`). The specified refusal message is `run the full review: the diff or chunking changed`. In that string `diff` is immediately followed by ` or`, so the contiguous substring `diff changed` does **not** occur. Given the input in this test (re-run of `T1`/`critic` after rewriting `c.py`), a conforming implementation refuses with the specified message and this assertion fails even though the behavior is correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_rechunk.py: `test_a_changed_diff_is_refused_before_any_reviewer_runs`

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `"max_chunk_chars" in out.reason`. The design's refusal message for this case is again `run the full review: the diff or chunking changed`, which never names the field. With the test's input (config `max_chunk_chars` changed 150 → 4000, same diff and reviewer), a conforming implementation emits the specified message, the literal `max_chunk_chars` is absent, and the assertion fails. (The same message is shared with the diff case per the design, so at most one of these two field-specific substrings could appear, and in fact neither does.)
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_rechunk.py: `test_a_changed_chunk_size_is_refused`

chunk_findings.detail: The guard reads the recorded chunk size from the evidence key `"chunk_chars"`, but the design/schema for the evidence this change records calls that field `max_chunk_chars` (point (1): "evidence of every ddflow review gains diff_sha …, max_chunk_chars, reviewed …"). Every other field the validator reads matches the design's name (`diff_sha`, `reviewed`), so this is the odd one out: `prior.get("chunk_chars")` returns `None` for a record written by the full run (which stores `max_chunk_chars`). The comparison then evaluates `mine[0].max_chunk_chars != None`, which is `True` for any reviewer whose `max_chunk_chars` is set, and the function returns the refusal "…max_chunk_chars is X now, None when <id>.<gate> was recorded: the chunks differ, run the full review" (exit 3). Concrete case: run a full `ddflow review <id> --gate G` with a reviewer configured `max_chunk_chars = 40000`, then `ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk 2` — the diff and chunking are unchanged, yet the merge is refused, so the feature never does what it exists for. If (and only if) the writer side in a later part stores the value under `chunk_chars`, this is a no-op; on the stated schema it breaks every `--chunk` call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py — `_rerun_scope` (`mine[0].max_chunk_chars != prior.get("chunk_chars")`)

chunk_findings.detail: A rerun that ends in `R.ERROR` skips the merge and then falls straight through to `results.append(res)`. The fact that the condition must exclude `R.ERROR` is itself the evidence that errored results reach the normal append/record path: the preceding code for a chunk rerun has already replaced `revs` with the single matching reviewer, so `results` holds exactly the errored `res`, `best = min(results, ...)` is that errored result, and the gate's record is written from it — un-merged. Concretely: gate `G` holds a recorded full review of diff `D` with `reviewed=[1,2,3,4]` and findings for chunks 1–4; the user runs `ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk 3` and the chunk-3 model call fails (`res.status == R.ERROR`). The new record now contains only the errored chunk-3 rerun and drops chunks 1,2,4's `reviewed`/`findings`, which contradicts the stated merge rule ("outcome recomputed as a full run would" — a full run that errors on one chunk still keeps the other chunks' findings). Worse, it defeats the point of the change: if the errored result does not carry `diff_sha`/`max_chunk_chars`/`reviewed` consistent with the prior record, the *next* `--chunk` attempt fails the `_rerun_scope` match and forces exactly the 25–40 min full review this feature was meant to eliminate. The check also fails to achieve its own comment ("a record is not overwritten blind"): the record is still overwritten, just with strictly less data. Either return early on `R.ERROR` without touching the record, or merge prior findings for the non-rerun chunks before writing.

chunk_findings.detail: The stated design is that `diff_sha` is the sha256 of the *hunk-context-stripped* diff, and the line just above computes exactly that value into the local `stripped` (`stripped = strip_hunk_context(diff)`) and then chunks on it (`split_diff(stripped, ...)`). Because the chunking is done on `stripped`, both the number of chunks (`1..N`) and each chunk's contents are independent of the unchanged context lines around the edit. But the digest is computed over the original `diff`, not over `stripped`. So for two diffs that contain the same +/- changes and differ only in surrounding context (the canonical case being a diff regenerated with a different context width, e.g. `git diff -U10` vs the default `-U3`, or after unrelated lines nearby shift), `split_diff` produces byte-identical chunks and identical numbering, yet `diff_sha` differs from the value recorded by the full review. The user then runs `ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk N`, the chunk review itself succeeds (the numbers are valid), and the merge in design step (3) compares `diff_sha`, sees a mismatch, and refuses with "run the full review: the diff or chunking changed" — forcing exactly the 25–40 minute full re-run (or the unverifiable out-of-band call) that this change exists to avoid, even though the chunking over which the re-review was requested is unchanged. Passing `stripped` (the same value used for `split_diff`) to `diff_digest` would make the evidence's `diff_sha` context-independent as designed and let the merge proceed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:1402 (`res.diff_sha, res.chunk_chars = diff_digest(diff), rev.max_chunk_chars`)

chunk_findings.detail: The re-run merge validates its "same cut" precondition by reading `prior.get("chunk_chars")` (and `res.chunk_chars`), and rebuilds the kept findings from `prior.get("chunk_findings", [])`, but the evidence a ddflow review records uses the names stated in the design: the background size is stored as `max_chunk_chars`, and the findings-with-chunk-number are stored as `findings` (item 1: "evidence ... gains diff_sha ..., max_chunk_chars, reviewed ... and findings with their chunk number"). Concretely, take the very scenario the change exists for: the gate's latest record is a real full review of a 5-chunk diff with `max_chunk_chars = 131072`, and the user runs `ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk 3`. In `merge_rerun`, `prior.get("chunk_chars")` returns `None` while `mine` is the integer chunk size, so the first guard loop returns the refusal `"...differs in chunk_chars (None vs 131072)..."`, the CLI exits 3 with "run the full review", and the 25–40 min full re-run (or an out-of-band call ddflow cannot verify) is forced again — exactly bug Bd2332f8f2a. Even if that guard were by some chance satisfied, `prior.get("chunk_findings", [])` would be empty, so the merged record would contain only the re-run chunk's findings and every earlier chunk's kept findings would be silently dropped, contradicting item 3's "findings = earlier chunks' kept + re-run chunks' replaced". (If the `ReviewResult` attribute is likewise named `max_chunk_chars`, the same mismatch surfaces earlier as an `AttributeError` on `res.chunk_chars`.) Tests that hand-build a `prior` dict using the same names the merge reads would not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:merge_rerun

chunk_findings.detail: The change specifies the MCP argument as `chunks` ("MCP ddflow_review 'chunks'"), and the API lambda passes that value as `chunks=`. However, the tool registers the parameter under the singular name `"chunk"` and reads it back with `a.get("chunk")`. A client that follows the specified MCP interface and calls `ddflow_review(repo, gate, chunks=[5])` therefore has its argument either rejected as unknown or dropped; `a.get("chunk")` returns `None`, so `chunks=None` is forwarded to the review core. `None` is the sentinel for a full review, so instead of re-reviewing chunk 5 and merging it into the recorded gate outcome, the call silently performs the entire 25–40 minute review — exactly the behavior this change exists to avoid — and never exercises the merge/refusal path at all. To demonstrate: invoke the MCP review with `chunks=[5]` against a gate whose last record is a ddflow review of the same diff; the argument is not seen, a full review runs, and no chunk-specific merge occurs.

data.body: Part 1 (B-fix-review-chunks, bde10e6) names every unreviewed chunk with its files. Part 2: 'ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk N' (repeatable, or '2,5'; MCP ddflow_review property 'chunk', an array -- singular to match the CLI flag, as the parity ratchet requires) re-reviews only those chunks and merges into the gate's recorded review. Evidence of every review now carries diff_sha (sha256 of the hunk-context-stripped diff), max_chunk_chars, chunks_total, reviewed (chunk numbers) and chunk_findings (findings with their chunk; detail capped at 2000). A re-run is checked BEFORE any reviewer call: an item, a recorded review with per-chunk evidence, the same diff_sha, the same reviewer, the same max_chunk_chars, chunk numbers in range -- else refused (exit 3) without recording. Merged: reviewed = union; earlier chunks' findings kept, re-run chunks' replaced; unreviewed = the rest with their earlier reasons; off-contract count kept; outcome recomputed as a full run would. An errored re-run is refused unrecorded. Also fixes Baf7d5082f5 (a template syntax error escaped prompts.render as a jinja2 exception).

chunk_findings.detail:
The hunk deletes the only assignment that produced the chunk prompt's rule text:

```python
-    rules = "\n\n".join(r.strip() for r in (rev.extra_rules, extra_rules) if r.strip())
```

and replaces it with the `wanted/outside/res.requested` block. Nothing in the hunk re-binds `rules`, yet the prompt construction that the very next line imports (`from ..services import prompts as P`) renders the per-chunk prompt from that value. The old docstring states the contract explicitly — "`extra_rules` adds to the reviewer's own `extra_rules`" — so `rules` was consumed by `P.render(...)`. With the new signature (`extra_rules` replaced by `only`) the caller-supplied portion may legitimately go away, but the reviewer's own `rev.extra_rules` has to keep being applied; simply deleting the line does not do that.

Concretely: run `ddflow review <id> --gate G` (or `--chunk 2`) on any diff. Execution reaches `run_review`, computes `wanted`/`outside`, then hits the `P.render(...)` call for the chunk prompt where `rules` is now an undefined name, raising `NameError: name 'rules' is not defined` before any reviewer is invoked — so no chunk is ever reviewed and the gate records nothing. If the render call was instead edited to take `rev.extra_rules` directly (not shown in this part), then the reviewer's configured `extra_rules` are silently dropped from every chunk prompt, which is a behavior regression of the same line.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/services/review.py — run_review (the deleted `rules = ...` line, just above `from ..services import prompts as P`)

chunk_findings.detail: The system-prompt render no longer receives the value the function computed for this prompt: `rules` has been replaced with the raw `rev.extra_rules.strip()`. These are not interchangeable — `rules` is the assembled rules string the surrounding code built for exactly this call (it is the reason `.strip()` was written on it), whereas `rev.extra_rules` is only the per-invocation extra. Whatever `rules` composed beyond the raw field is now silently dropped from the system prompt. The concrete case this feature depends on is a chunk re-run: `ddflow review <id> --gate G --chunk 2` is supposed to tell the reviewer to review only the named chunks, and that directive is part of the rules passed to `render`; with `rev.extra_rules.strip()` the reviewer is given the un-scoped rules, so it reviews the whole diff, and the merge keeps only chunk 2's findings while discarding the freshly produced findings for the other chunks (the `reviewed`/`chunk_findings` evidence still claims only chunk 2 was re-run). The same loss occurs for any review that relied on the default/project-derived portion of `rules`: a plain `ddflow review <id>` with no `--extra-rules` now renders the system template with an empty `extra_rules` instead of the composed rules. Restore `extra_rules=rules` (or make `rules` and `rev.extra_rules.strip()` provably identical) to avoid changing the reviewer's instructions.

chunk_findings.detail: The following `if why:` guard treats a falsy reason string as a successful merge. A reviewer result can have `status == R.ERROR` with an empty `reason` (the pre-change logging code explicitly handles `res.reason` being falsy, e.g. `... + (f" — {res.reason}" if res.reason else "")`). For such a result, `why = ""`, so the refusal branch is skipped: the errored result is appended to `results` and execution continues toward recording the re-run, contradicting the stated intent "An errored re-run is refused unrecorded." The condition should test `res.status == R.ERROR` unconditionally (or `if res.status == R.ERROR or why:`), not via the truthiness of the reason string.

chunk_findings.detail: The hunk deletes the only binding of the local `rules` (the value that combined the reviewer's own `rev.extra_rules` with the caller-supplied `extra_rules`), and replaces it in place with the chunk-selection code. Nothing in the function re-binds `rules`. The prompt is rendered a few lines further down (the `from ..services import prompts as P` line that immediately follows the hunk is there to render the reviewer prompt, and it is precisely `rules` that the prompt consumed — that is why the removed line merged `rev.extra_rules` with `extra_rules`). Consequently, on the very first call to `review_diff` the interpreter reaches the render call with `rules` unbound and raises `NameError: name 'rules' is not defined`, so no review — full-run or `--chunk` re-run — can complete. In addition, the signature swap `extra_rules: str = ""` → `only: list[int] | None = None` in the same position means any existing caller that passes the documented `extra_rules=` argument now dies with `TypeError: review_diff() got an unexpected keyword argument 'extra_rules'`, and any caller that passes it positionally has the string bound to `only`, where `sorted(set(only or ()))` turns it into a list of characters and the range check then returns the bogus `ERROR` "no chunk [' ', 'e', ...] -- this diff has chunks 1..N". The intent describes only re-review/merge behavior and says nothing about dropping `extra_rules` support, so the removal is not a deliberate, accounted-for change.

data.body: Decision D-review-triage (operator 2026-10-02, option C): a review that reports findings stays recorded failed (D-failed-critic-not-blocking stands); no new gate outcome, no new completion block. Each finding of a recorded review gets a stable number N (its place in the evidence's chunk_findings, printed as #N by ddflow review) and a digest of its full text (severity, location, title, detail). 'ddflow review triage <id> --gate G --finding N --refuted|--confirmed --probe <evidence>' (CLI; MCP ddflow_review_triage) appends one review.triaged event per finding: refuted = the probe that shows it false; confirmed = the fix/test that answers it. Folded per item+gate by digest, so a re-review (full or --chunk) carries a triage over ONLY when the finding text is identical. gate status and show print, under a gate with findings, '3 finding(s): 2 refuted, 1 confirmed, 0 untriaged'; the gate outcome is untouched. Refused: no ddflow review with per-chunk findings on record, N out of range, no verdict or both, an empty probe.

chunk_findings.detail:
The number printed by `ddflow review` is restarted for every element of the outer `for res in ...` loop (the loop that prints `res.label`, `res.coverage()`, `res.elapsed_s`), while `triage()` treats `N` as a *flat, review-wide* index into the recorded `chunk_findings` (`f = found[finding - 1]`, and the refusal text `#1..##{len(found)}`). These two numbering schemes only agree when the review produced a single result item. Concrete failure: a review whose evidence `chunk_findings` is `[A1, A2, B1]` (two chunks/results with findings) prints

    <label A>: 2 finding(s), ...
      #1 [high] a.py:1
      #2 [low]  a.py:9
    <label B>: 1 finding(s), ...
      #1 [high] b.py:42

so the operator triaging `ddflow review triage <id> --gate critic --finding 1 --refuted --probe ...` after reading B's `#1` resolves to `found[0]` = `A1`; the event records `A1`'s digest (and `A1`'s severity/title/location) with the verdict meant for `B1`. `A1` is shown as refuted/confirmed and `B1` stays untriaged, i.e. the log states the wrong finding's fate, and because the fold is by digest the wrong verdict is carried over on re-review. The printed number should be a single running counter over all results (or `triage` should take the chunk qualified number), so that the `#N` a user sees always equals the `chunk_findings` position `triage` indexes.

chunk_findings.detail:
The spec for this change lists "no verdict or both" among the **refused** cases, and every other refusal (no recorded review, N out of range, empty probe, no verdict) is produced by `A.triage` and propagated verbatim via `if out.exit != OK: ... return out.exit`, i.e. as the framework's `REFUSED` code. The one case this function special-cases locally — both `--refuted` and `--confirmed` — is instead returned as `FAIL`. Concretely, running

    ddflow review triage <id> --gate G --finding 1 --refuted --confirmed --probe "x"

exits with `FAIL`, while passing `--finding 1 --probe "x"` (no verdict) or `--finding 99 --refuted --probe "x"` (out of range) exits with `REFUSED` for the same "this operation is refused" class. Any caller that branches on the distinct `REFUSED` exit (scripts, gate status classification) will mis-handle the both-verdicts input, and the CLI and the MCP path (`A.triage` directly, if it performs its own exclusivity check) disagree on the outcome for identical input. The exclusivity guard should return `REFUSED` to match the documented contract and the surrounding refusal paths.

chunk_findings.detail: The printer numbers findings with a counter that restarts inside the per-result loop (`for n, f in enumerate(res.findings, 1)`), but `triage()` interprets `--finding N` as an index into the single gate-level list `rec.evidence["chunk_findings"]` (`f = found[finding - 1]`). When a recorded review contains more than one result carrying findings (e.g. a multi-chunk/multi-reviewer review), each result re-prints "#1", "#2", … while the triage list is a single flat sequence. Concretely: chunk A yields finding X and chunk B yields finding Y; the user sees `#1 [..] X` and `#1 [..] Y`, runs `ddflow review triage <id> --gate critic --finding 1 --refuted --probe ...` intending Y, and line `f = found[finding - 1]` records the verdict/probe against X's digest instead (and reports "finding #1 ... X"); Y is left untriaged. The number printed as `#N` therefore does not identify the finding that `--finding N` acts on whenever the review has more than one result with findings, contradicting the stated contract that N is "its place in the evidence's chunk_findings".

chunk_findings.detail:
Changing the `id` positional from `nargs="?"` to `nargs="*"` makes the new `triage <id>` verb order-sensitive, because argparse consumes positional runs *around* optionals: each contiguous `A…` run is matched separately against the remaining positional actions, and once `consume_positionals` has used up the `id` action it is removed from the list, so a later positional run cannot be absorbed by it.

Concretely, `ddflow review triage --gate critic 123` builds the arg pattern `A O A A` (`triage`=A, `--gate`=O, `critic`=A, `123`=A). Argparse consumes `triage` as the single positional (the nargs='*' pattern `(-*[A-]*)` stops at the `O`), then consumes `--gate critic` as the optional, leaving `123` with no positional action to receive it; the parser exits with `unrecognized arguments: 123` and never reaches `cmd_review`/`_triage`. The same happens for any invocation that puts the item after a flag, e.g. `ddflow review triage --finding 3 --refuted --probe x 123`.

The adjacent form documented in the synopsis (`ddflow review triage <id> --gate G …`, pattern `A A O …`) does work, so the failure is specific to the id-after-flags ordering — a plausible way to invoke a verb-then-item CLI (`cmd verb --flags item`), which now fails outright instead of triaging. This is introduced by this change: with the old `nargs="?"` (single positional) all orderings worked, and the two-token `triage <id>` is only handled correctly while the two tokens remain contiguous.

evidence.note: Probed: review verb argparse (review --gate critic T1 and review T1 --gate critic unchanged; 'triage --gate c T1' is not supported, same as every verb+item command); old records without digests refuse triage with a reason and show no triage line; a chunk re-run and a full re-review keep triage for identical text only; duplicates and multi-reviewer ambiguity found by critic and fixed with tests that fail on c459c09.

counting and the line format live once in gates.triage_counts/triage_line (status, show, api all use them); the finding digest in one finding_digest; no second renderer for gate status vs show (both use GateStatus.render)

chunk_findings.detail:
The digests of word-for-word identical findings are assigned *by position in `res.findings`*, not by content, and `_tell_duplicates_apart` strips any existing `-N` suffix (`base = f.digest.split("-")[0]`) and reassigns it from the current list order. Position is not stable across a `--chunk` re-review: the merge rebuilds `res.findings` from the kept chunks' stored `chunk_findings` (line ~1566) and then the re-reviewed chunk's findings are appended by `_review_chunk`, so a re-reviewed *earlier* chunk's finding moves after a later chunk's finding, reversing their relative order.

Concrete failure: a review reports the same text (severity/location/title/detail) once in chunk 1 and once in chunk 3, so they get digests `abc` (#1) and `abc-2` (#3). Record `ddflow review triage <id> --gate critic --finding 1 --refuted --probe "..."` → event keyed by `abc`. Then run `ddflow review <id> --gate critic --chunk 1`. The merge lays out the kept chunk-3 finding (`abc-2`) first and the new chunk-1 finding (`abc`) last; `_tell_duplicates_apart` walks that order and reassigns chunk-3 → `abc`, chunk-1 → `abc-2`. The refutation recorded for digest `abc` (finding #1) now folds onto the chunk-3 finding, and finding #1 shows untriaged — even though the finding text is unchanged. This contradicts the stated invariant that a re-review "carries a triage over only when the finding text is identical": here the text *is* identical, yet the triage lands on a different finding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py `_tell_duplicates_apart` (called from `_settle`)

chunk_findings.detail: The CLI and MCP entry points for the same operation call two different names on the API layer. `_triage` calls `A.triage(...)`, while the MCP tool `ddflow_review_triage` calls `_api().review_triage(...)` (ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py). Every other tool in this codebase uses the same function name in both surfaces (e.g. `cmd_review` calls `A.review`, and the MCP `ddflow_review` entry uses `_api().review`), so these two are supposed to resolve to one API function. Unless the API module defines both `triage` and `review_triage` (in which case one is dead/aliased), one of the two calls raises `AttributeError`. Concretely, running `ddflow review triage <id> --gate critic --finding 1 --refuted --probe p` will crash inside `_triage` if the API only exposes `review_triage` (the name the MCP tool and the tool name `ddflow_review_triage` use); conversely the MCP tool is broken if the API only exposes `triage`. Either way one documented entry point for this feature cannot work.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/review.py (`_triage`, the `A.triage(...)` call)

chunk_findings.detail: `_say_result` numbers findings with `enumerate(res.findings, 1)`, i.e. the finding's *position within the result object of the current run*, while `triage()` resolves `--finding N` against the recorded evidence's `chunk_findings` (`f = found[finding - 1]`). These two orderings only coincide for a full review. For a `--chunk` re-review the displayed result contains only the re-run chunks' findings, so they start at `#1` again, but the recorded `chunk_findings` is the merged full set. Concretely: an initial full review records 5 findings into `evidence["chunk_findings"]` (indices 0–4). A later `ddflow review X --gate critic --chunk 4` re-runs chunk 4, which has one finding; `_say_result` prints it as `#1 [severity] ...`, and with several reviewers `_say_triage_scope` even announces `#1..#1`. But `triage(X, gate="critic", finding=1, ...)` passes the range check against `len(chunk_findings) == 5` and appends a `review.triaged` event with `digest = chunk_findings[0]["digest"]` — the chunk-1 finding, not the chunk-4 finding the user actually saw as `#1`. The verdict/probe is therefore recorded against the wrong finding's digest, and the digest-based carry-over in a subsequent re-review will attach that triage to the wrong finding. The two places must number identically (the scope message/`_say_result` must print the evidence position, not the per-run index) for `--finding N` to address what `ddflow review` printed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py `_say_result` / `_say_triage_scope`

chunk_findings.detail:
`_tell_duplicates_apart` recomputes each digest's base with `base = f.digest.split("-")[0]`, so it does not merely disambiguate the findings of *one* review — it renumbers every finding in `res.findings`, including findings carried over from earlier chunks by a `--chunk` re-review (those arrive via the merge path with `digest=f.get("digest", "")`, i.e. already ending in `-2`, `-3`, …). A carried finding that was the second copy of a duplicate had its recorded digest `abc-2`; if the first copy lived in the chunk that is now being re-reviewed and comes back with different text (or no finding at all), the base `abc` becomes free again and the untouched finding is silently rewritten to `abc`. Because triage is folded *by digest* ("Folded per item+gate by digest"), the recorded triage event still points at `abc-2` and no longer matches any finding, so the verdict is lost; in the converse ordering a `confirmed` recorded against the re-reviewed finding's old digest can land on the untouched chunk's finding.

Repro: (1) an item whose reviewer reports the *same* finding text in chunk 1 and chunk 2; `ddflow review` records them with digests `d` (chunk 1) and `d-2` (chunk 2). (2) `ddflow review triage <id> --gate critic --finding 2 --refuted --probe …` records a triage against digest `d-2`. (3) `ddflow review <id> --chunk 1` re-reviews only chunk 1 and the reviewer now reports a different finding there. The merge carries the chunk-2 finding with digest `d-2`; `_settle` → `_tell_duplicates_apart` sees `base = "d"`, `seen["d"] == 1`, and sets `f.digest = "d"`. The persisted chunk-2 digest is now `d`, the triage event still says `d-2`, and chunk 2 shows up untriaged even though its text never changed. The same reset happens when it is the *only* remaining finding with that base, so it is not merely an ordering artefact.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py `_tell_duplicates_apart` (called from `_settle`)

chunk_findings.detail: The CLI entry point for the new operation calls `A.triage(...)`, but the MCP entry point for the same operation calls `_api().review_triage(...)`. For every other command the two surfaces agree on the api-layer attribute name: the CLI's `cmd_review` calls `A.review(...)` and the MCP `ddflow_review` handler calls `_api().review(...)`, so `A` and `_api()` are the same module/namespace and the attribute is the bare command name (`review`). With one api-layer function there can be only one attribute, so one of these two call sites is wrong: if the api defines `review_triage` (consistent with the tool name `ddflow_review_triage` and with MCP), then `ddflow review triage <id> --gate G --finding 1 --refuted --probe p` raises `AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'triage'` before any event is recorded; if it defines `triage`, the MCP tool `ddflow_review_triage` raises `AttributeError` instead. There is no input that makes both work unless the api layer happens to export both names/aliases, which is inconsistent with the naming used by every adjacent command. One of the two documented front-ends to `A.triage`/`review_triage` is therefore broken on every invocation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/review.py `_triage` (the `A.triage(...)` call) vs ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py `ddflow_review_triage` (the `_api().review_triage(...)` call)

chunk_findings.detail: The test tries to prove that a `--chunk` re-review keeps the triage of findings outside the re-run chunk, but it cannot fail. It discards the result of `api.review(repo, gate="critic", item="T1", chunks=[second])` and only asserts `G.triage_counts(...)["refuted"] == 2`. Because the re-run uses the very same `wording` (only `a.py` words finding #1, and that chunk is never re-run), the `b.py` finding's text/digest is unchanged, so its refuted triage is retained by the digest rule, and the untouched `a.py` finding is trivially retained. Concretely: if `api.review` rejects the `chunks` argument (returns FAIL, state untouched) the assertion still passes; if `chunks` is silently ignored and every chunk is re-reviewed the wording is identical so both triages are still retained by digest, and the assertion still passes. To make the assertion capable of being false the touched chunk's finding would have to change wording (losing its own triage, leaving `refuted == 1`) while the untouched chunk keeps its triage; as written no input distinguishes a correct chunk-scoped re-review from a broken or ignored one.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_triage.py::test_a_chunk_rerun_keeps_the_triage_of_the_findings_it_did_not_touch

chunk_findings.detail: `assert json.dumps(out.data["counts"])` is always truthy: `json.dumps` returns a non-empty string for any dict (and raises rather than returning falsy for unserializable values), so this line asserts nothing about the recorded counts. The surrounding checks on `out.data["counts"]["confirmed"]` and the event fields are meaningful, but this particular assertion can never fail and provides no protection.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_triage.py::test_the_mcp_tool_records_the_same_event

data.claim: Real and fixed (5528393): a positional digest suffix for duplicate findings moves a triage to the wrong copy when an earlier chunk is re-reviewed (3 reviewers) -- dropped; identical findings are one claim, triaged together. Weak test of the chunk re-run and an always-true assert -- strengthened/removed. Refuted: (1) 'A.triage vs _api().review_triage is an AttributeError' -- A is the ddflow.api.review submodule (function triage), _api() the package (re-export review_triage); test_the_cli_verb_* and test_the_mcp_tool_* run both. (2) '--chunk prints per-run #N, not the merged record's' -- merge_rerun replaces res.findings with the merged list before printing; the strengthened test asserts #1,#2 after re-running one chunk of two. Kept as documented limitation: with several reviewers, triage addresses the recorded reviewer's findings (the output's last line names it; MCP description says so).
data.falsifier: the CLI or MCP triage raises AttributeError, or a chunk re-run prints #1 for a finding that is #2 in the record
data.probe: pytest tests/test_review_triage.py (CLI subprocess + MCP spec['api'] + chunk rerun)
